requirements.requirement: A persistent host firewall is enabled on node1 and survives restart.
requirements.summary: UFW was active and enabled with a default inbound REJECT policy before restart. A bounded restart was acknowledged and observed, the boot ID changed, and the recovered node again showed UFW active, enabled, and carrying the persisted policy and rules. The fixed lifecycle boot identities independently confirm the restart.

requirements.requirement: Inbound SSH and TCP port 8080 are permitted.
requirements.summary: UFW contains IPv4 and IPv6 allow rules for TCP 22 and 8080. Direct IPv4 connection tests reached active listeners on both ports before and after restart, with matching firewall counters.
The firewall has a default inbound REJECT policy. Direct tests against an active listener on unrelated TCP port 18081 were rejected before and after restart, while reject-chain counters increased.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied. The firewall is persistent across an observed restart, permits SSH and TCP 8080, and directly rejects unrelated inbound TCP traffic. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete and coherent for node1. Operational hygiene is strong apart from minor retained /tmp test artifacts and a corrected temporary-listener cleanup issue.
limitations: Direct connection testing exercised IPv4 only; IPv6 coverage is supported by the configured UFW rules and enabled IPv6 setting but was not behaviorally tested.

Rejection behavior was sampled using TCP port 18081 rather than exhaustively probing all unrelated inbound ports; the observed default REJECT policy and reject-chain counters provide supporting general coverage.

operational_hygiene.summary: No causally unrelated state-changing command was identified: firewall changes established the requested state; namespaces, veth interfaces, and listeners supported bounded behavior tests; the restart validated persistence and fulfilled the mandatory protocol; later mutations corrected cleanup failures. The second probe initially left its temporary HTTP listeners running, and two cleanup attempts failed, but the processes were subsequently terminated and the final check found no test listeners or namespace. Five fwproof log/error files from the probes remained under /tmp, constituting minor abandoned residue. No failed services or package damage were observed.
